svg.text: Compress 384-dim vectors to bits — and still find what you need

g.text: Multiply by random Gaussian matrix R (seeded, deterministic)
Keep only the sign: positive → 1, negative → 0
Low distance = similar vectors. 1 CPU instruction per 64 bits.
1. Normalize vector (store L2 norm), then rotate with random orthogonal matrix Q
Q is generated via Gram-Schmidt on a Gaussian matrix (seeded, deterministic)
2. Quantize each coordinate with Lloyd-Max codebook (8 centroids for 3-bit)
Lloyd-Max optimal centroids for N(0,1), scaled by 1/√d
Each coordinate snaps to its nearest centroid → 3-bit index (0-7)
384 x 3 bits = 144 bytes + 4 bytes norm = 148 bytes (10x smaller!)
Similarity = dot product in rotated domain via codebook lookups. Since Q is orthogonal,
⟨x, y⟩ = ⟨Qx, Qy⟩. No matrix multiply at search time — just table lookups!
QJL eliminates 98% of candidates with XOR + popcount — nanoseconds per vector.
TurboQuant_mse re-ranks 200 survivors with near-optimal accuracy (MSE ≤ 0.038 at 3-bit).
Result: near-exact recall at a fraction of brute-force cost.
10,000 docs: 15 MB raw → 1.9 MB compressed (QJL + TurboQuant_mse 3-bit)
